text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- If the Neretva canton fails to form a joint police force, a scheduled meeting on Monday between chairman of Bosnian presidency Alija Izetbegovic and Croatian president Franjo Tudjman will be postponed, an official from Izetbegovic's office said.

- Deputy to the High Representative in Bosnia, Michael Steiner, said after holding talks with Croatian president that Tudjman was abstract regarding Bosnia and he failed to promise anything concrete except a vague statement about supporting the implementation of the Dayton peace treaty.
- Co-chairman in the Bosnian Council of Ministers, Haris Silajdzic, asked London Club of creditors to consider material damage caused by war when rescheduling Bosnian debt.
- Bosnian delegation expects to negotiate 90 percent forgiveness of the country's debt, Silajdzic said.
- Due to repeated postponment of the donors' conference the process of post-war reconstruction has been delayed, Moslem-Croat federation prime minister Edhem Bicakcic told Council of Europe.
- Two-day summit of the Organisation of Islamic Countries (OIC) convenes in Sarajevo to discuss reconstruction needs with Bosnian authorities.
- Izetbegovic has accepted an invitation for talks with Macedonian president Kiro Gligorov but a date for the visit has not been confirmed.
- Families identified 23 of 82 bodies on Thursday which were exhumated from a mass grave in the Sarajevo suburb of Vlakovo.

- Bosnian Serb representatives have been invited to attend the OIC conference but they remain doubtful about the intentions of the Islamic countries and will not participate, Husein Zivalj, deputy foreign minister, says. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
